title: How to Make a Nintendo 64 Game in 2026
content_html:
— Tuesday, August 4th 2026

Two years ago, I was Porting my JavaScript Game Engine to C for No Reason. I have since found a reason: making a new N64 game!

The result is Xibalba 64 – a Wolfenstein 3D-like FPS. Modretro agreed to publish the game as a physical launch title for their M64 (a modern N64 clone), complete with cartridge, packaging and manual!

Xibalba 64 on Modretro.com

This, to my knowledge, is only the second physical release of any new N64 game since the end of the console's original commercial life. The infamous Xeno Crisis by Bitmap Bureau – originally a new game for the Sega Mega Drive and subsequently released on many, many more consoles – came to the N64 in 2023. No other new games have been published for the N64 since Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 in 2002.

The Engine

Impact was a JavaScript game engine I developed back in 2010. It was tailored for 2D action games, handling tile sheets, background maps, sprites and collision detection. It's very simple, but still a sound foundation for whatever you want to throw at it.

Two years ago I rewrote Impact in C. Why? I don't know. It was fun.

This C port, high_impact, has a notion of a “platform backend”. The platform handles the low-level plumbing – opening a window, creating a drawing surface, reading input, etc. Out of the box, high_impact comes with two platform backends (SDL2 and Sokol), and you can compile your game for either one. This already enables high_impact games to run on many different devices.

The rendering backend in high_impact is also modular. You can compile your game with a software renderer, OpenGL or Metal (for iOS/macOS). Support for new platform backends or rendering backends can be added without modifying any other part of the engine.

A perfect starting point for an N64 game.

N64 Hardware and Platform Library

The N64 is a quirky beast. In addition to the 93 MHz MIPS CPU (big-endian!), it has two coprocessors for handling graphics, sound and more:

  • “Reality Display Processor” (RDP) – a fixed-function graphics processor
  • “Reality Signal Processor” (RSP) – a programmable vector processor

Both of these live in the same physical package, commonly called the “Reality Coprocessor” (RCP).

Image from the N64Brew Wiki

For the first few years of the N64's life, Nintendo closely guarded access to the RSP. It was exclusively used by Nintendo's officially sanctioned platform library, “libultra”. Only later did Nintendo allow game studios to write custom “microcode” (actually just MIPS assembly) for the RSP.

Keeping the hardware happy is no simple feat, and the instructions for the RDP are quirky and complicated. Programming your game on bare metal is pretty much out of the question. In recent years, Nintendo's official “libultra” has made its way onto the internet, but using it would risk a copyright lawsuit.

Luckily, the N64 homebrew scene has picked up a lot of steam in the last few years and we have a very capable alternative now: Libdragon.

Libdragon is basically SDL for the N64. It provides facilities for drawing sprites and triangles, sound output, controller input and much more.

It took me only a few evenings to build a new platform backend for high_impact on top of libdragon. I tested this with Biolab Disaster. The game code remained unmodified; performance was meh, but I was using the N64 hardware in the most naive way possible.

Dev Environment

Libdragon provides the compilers and everything else that's necessary to build a ROM file for the N64. The installation instructions and all other documentation are comprehensive and well-written. The library comes with many examples to get you started.

In general, it was a pleasure to work with Libdragon. Just a heads up: you probably want to use the preview branch as the “stable” trunk branch has hopelessly fallen behind.

For testing, a good emulator is invaluable. For the longest time, N64 emulation was extremely inaccurate. Lackluster emulation of the RSP and RDP coprocessors, in particular, was the cause of most problems.

Most emulators just emulated Nintendo's platform library, libultra. They emulated the intent to draw a triangle, not what the hardware would actually do. While inaccurate, this made emulation possible at all in the early days. Famously, UltraHLE (“Ultra High Level Emulator”) was released well within the lifetime of the N64 and caused a lot of headaches and subsequent lawsuits.

These days the N64 core in Ares is much closer to the actual hardware – the RDP and RSP are fully emulated, including accurate timing for the RSP. The infamous slow memory bandwidth of the N64, however, can still only be tested on real hardware (which recently caused me some disappointment).

So you need a real N64 and a cartridge that lets you play arbitrary .z64 ROM files. The open-source SummerCart64 is excellent and available from many different manufacturers. Be aware: some manufacturers (especially on AliExpress) cheap out on the components of the board.

SummerCart64 has the usual SD card slot to store your ROMs, but what makes it great for development is its USB-C port: you can directly connect it to your PC and upload a ROM as part of your build process using sc64deployer.

I ended up with the N64 next to my PC, connected via USB, and used a cheap $10 USB analog capture card to display its video output in a window on my desktop. On Linux, it took some fiddling with mpv to get low-latency output; here's the script I used.

With this setup, iterating on real hardware was just a matter of compiling and pushing the N64 reset button.

The Game

I originally made Xibalba as a demo for my JavaScript game engine in 2014. WebGL was still the hot new thing back then; a 3D game in a browser was quite a novelty. The game was very short, featuring only a handful of levels, weapons and enemy types.

In contrast, I wanted Xibalba 64 to be a real game, not just a demo. So I not only needed to port the game to C and high_impact, but also expand on it with more levels, more enemy types and more weapons.

high_impact is a 2D game engine, but Xibalba 64 is clearly 3D. Well, not quite. Since the game has no elevation, it can be mostly treated as 2D. You could conceptually play Xibalba 64 from a 2D top-down perspective. Of course, that wouldn't be as exciting, but all the physics, movement and shooting would work the same way. In this regard, the game is very similar to Wolfenstein 3D.

Many of high_impact's physics functions expect a vec2_t argument with .x and .y components. But for drawing, I absolutely needed a 3D position, so I came up with this definition for a vec3_t type and changed the entity_t type:

typedef struct {
    float x, y;
} vec2_t;

typedef union {
    vec2_t xy;
    struct {
        float x, y, z;
    };
} vec3_t;

typedef struct {
    // ...
    vec3_t pos;
    vec3_t vel;
    // ...
} entity_t;

Now, whenever I need to call a function that accepts a vec2_t, I can “convert” from vec3_t for free:

trace_t res = trace(collision_map, entity->pos.xy, entity->vel.xy);

Since the inner vec3_t struct is “anonymous”, I can still access all values directly; i.e., entity->pos.z works just fine.

The initial port of the existing levels and enemy types went quite smoothly and was finished in about two weeks. I then spent another few months on extending the game and optimizing the renderer.

Most of Libdragon's functions fit naturally into a new platform and rendering backend, though I had to change some other parts of high_impact to bypass its mixer (Libdragon has its own, accelerated by the RSP) and image loader.

Throughout the whole process, I retained the ability to build the game with the SDL2 or Sokol backends. This was great for playtesting game logic and enemy behavior. To make levels, I also implemented a simple hot-reload mechanism triggered whenever a level file changed.

The level editor, bundled with high_impact, is a single self-contained HTML file. I ended up extending it quite a bit to add better support for lightmaps, display actual sprites for entities (instead of just boxes), add descriptions for entity settings and provide other small features. The single source of truth is still the C source code – the level editor reads it and extracts the entity types and supported settings automatically.

Since the level editor still works with JSON files, I built a small map compiler that reads the JSON and emits binary data. While loading JSON on the N64 is of course possible, it added some unnecessary ~100 ms of load time. So during the build process, each JSON level file is converted into a struct that essentially looks like this:

typedef struct {
    uint16_t magic;
    uint16_t entities_len;
    uint16_t map_width;
    uint16_t map_height;

    struct {
        uint16_t type_id;
        uint16_t x;
        uint16_t y;
        uint16_t settings_len;
        struct {
            uint16_t setting_type; // such as "name", "target", "size", ...
            union {
                float16_t float_value;
                int16_t int_value;
                struct {
                    int16_t string_len;
                    char string_value;
                };
            } value;
        } settings[settings_len];
    } entities[entities_len];

    uint16_t collision_map[map_width * map_height];
    uint16_t floor_map[map_width * map_height];
    uint16_t wall_map[map_width * map_height];
    uint16_t ceiling_map[map_width * map_height];
    uint16_t light_map[map_width * map_height];
} level_t;

The level compiler writes those values in big-endian format for the N64 and little-endian format for x86 (SDL2, Sokol, WASM), so we can easily read everything on all platforms without byte swapping.

Rendering

Libdragon itself has a function for drawing triangles: rdpq_triangle() inserts a single triangle draw call into the RDP queue. While this works, what you really want to do is submit your draw calls to the RSP, have some custom microcode to perform transformations, lighting, depth calculations, etc., and then let the RSP instruct the RDP to ultimately draw the triangle.

The intricacies of the RDP and RSP were still new to me, but luckily another outstanding open-source library, Tiny3D, handles all this and more with a simple-to-use API. Getting something on the screen was the easy part; making it performant was a whole other endeavor.

The N64 infamously only has 4 KB of texture memory. The largest textures you can upload are just a meager 64×64 pixels. Even worse, the memory latency for a texture upload is atrocious. One solution, used by Mario 64 and many other titles, is to render untextured polygons whenever you can.

This wouldn't really fly with the style of my game, so instead I had to be really careful with the draw order of level tiles to minimize texture uploads. On top of that, Tiny3D can load and submit up to 17 quads at once, and it would be wasteful not to use that. So I ended up collecting batches of triangles with the same texture in 64-bit draw calls:

typedef union render_call {
    uint64_t packed;
    uint32_t hashable;
    uint64_t ident : 46;
    struct {
        uint64_t translucent : 1;
        uint64_t texture_index : 9;
        uint64_t x : 10;
        uint64_t y : 10;
        uint64_t w : 8;
        uint64_t h : 8;
        uint64_t vbi : 14;
        uint64_t len : 4;
    };
} render_call_t;

Here vbi is the accompanying vertex buffer index, and len is the number of quads in this call. Since every call is just 64 bits wide, we can efficiently sort them at the end of the frame and issue them to Tiny3D.

But before I could do all this, I had to first figure out which parts of a level are actually visible. The original JavaScript Xibalba used a portal system, dividing each level into sectors and precomputing which sectors were visible from the current one. This worked fine, but produced a bit more overdraw than I would have liked.

So I opted for another approach: raycasting. Yes, the game is just casting 320 rays into the scene, covering the whole field of view. Each ray marks traversed tiles in a bitmap for submission to the renderer.

Later, I optimized the raycasting a bit more by recursively dividing the 320-pixel field of view until two rays hit the same tile. In this process, I also check whether any of the traversed tiles are missing a ceiling – if so, we have to draw a skybox.

Fun fact: the skybox in Xibalba 64 is just a single 32×32-pixel texture that is beautifully smeared across the horizon.

As another optimization, I arranged each tile sheet that wouldn't fit in a single upload into a single column and tried to use just 4-bit indexed colors wherever possible. Using fewer colors allowed more pixels to fit into texture memory, and the column layout ensured that each tile could be uploaded as a single, continuous chunk of memory.

With all of this, the game runs at a stable 60 FPS. Something not many other N64 games can claim!

The four-player split-screen mode doesn't quite hit the 60 FPS mark at all times, but still remains fluid. In contrast, GoldenEye 007 infamously often dropped into single-digit frame rates here.

Sound & Music

As with all my other games, my good friend Andreas Lösch produced some outstanding music. You can listen to the whole Xibalba 64 Soundtrack on Bandcamp.

The game itself also has a built-in music player that you can unlock in the single-player campaign.

Cartridge space is tight, and even compressed audio is typically either quite large or too expensive to decode.

In a heroic effort, Giovanni Bajo – one of the maintainers of Libdragon and an absolute wizard when it comes to anything N64 – implemented an RSP-accelerated Opus decoder. For context: Opus is an audio codec first published in 2012. That's 16 years(!) after the N64. It's a marvel that it works at all, but sadly it's still a bit too computationally expensive to be used during gameplay.

(Aside: Giovanni Bajo went on to implement a real-time H.264 decoder for the N64, too.)

The better option for now is a simple 4-bit VADPCM format that Libdragon transparently decodes on the RSP during playback. The compression ratio, of course, isn't great, but it's way better than uncompressed WAV. About 31 MB of the 32 MB ROM is used by sound and music.

After the release of Xibalba 64, I started to implement another audio compression format that would better address the space/quality/complexity trade-off. More on that in the next blog post!

Publishing & Sales

Modretro previously made a Game Boy Color clone – the Chromatic – compatible with all existing Game Boy and Game Boy Color games, and they were quite eager to publish many new games by hobbyist developers, too.

When they announced the M64, I thought this would be a great chance to get on board. As soon as I had a working prototype ready and was confident that I would be able to build the whole game (and make it good), I wrote an email to the generic Modretro customer service address and, to my surprise, heard back from the head of publishing within a day.

Bureaucracy was minimal and the contract was straightforward. I requested some changes that would allow me to release the game engine as open source later on, which Modretro was happy to accommodate.

Of course, as it goes with these projects, there were some delays and I only received a pre-production M64 late in the development process. But it didn't matter – the M64 worked as advertised; no changes to the game for the M64 were necessary.

Modretro also offered help with the box art, but another friend of mine was eager to do this instead. He later told me that, back in the '90s, he was responsible for the packaging of many titles published by Sierra in Germany, including Half-Life. So it's no surprise that the Xibalba 64 box art turned out great!

For the manual, I supplied text and illustrations to Modretro, and they laid it out for print. Smooth sailing. You can have a look at the PDF manual on the Xibalba 64 store page.

I'm not able to talk about sales numbers or my contract with Modretro in detail, and the game was released only a few days ago, but so far it's looking quite good. Of course, making N64 games will probably not let you quit your job, but it looks like it will pay for a few nice holidays.

Huge thanks to Giovanni Bajo of Libdragon, Max Bebök of Tiny3D, the entire N64brew Discord community and, of course, the Modretro team for pulling this off!

Here's the final trailer for the game.

Resources

If you're looking to get started with N64 development, these resources may help:

  • n64.dev – a collection of everything related to N64 development
  • N64brew Discord – a very friendly and helpful community; many of the library developers are here
  • Libdragon – the system library for the N64
  • Tiny3D – a simple and fast 3D graphics library
  • Pyrite64 – a visual editor and runtime for creating 3D games

So it's no surprise that the Xibalba 64 box art turned out great! For the manual, I supplied text and illustrations to Modretro, and they laid it out for print. Smooth sailing. You can have a look at the PDF manual on the Xibalba 64 store page. I'm not able to talk about sales numbers or my contract with Modretro in detail, and the game was released only a few days ago, but so far it's looking quite good. Of course, making N64 games will probably not let you quit your job, but it looks like it will pay for a few nice holidays. Huge thanks to Giovanni Bajo of Libdragon, Max Bebök of Tiny3D, the entire N64brew Discord community and, of course, the Modretro team for pulling this off! Here's the final trailer for the game. Resources If you're looking to get started with N64 development, these resources may help: n64.dev – a collection of everything related to N64 development N64brew Discord – a very friendly and helpful community; many of the library developers are here Libdragon – the system library for the N64 Tiny3D – a simple and fast 3D graphics library Pyrite64 – a visual editor and runtime for creating 3D games

sentences.zh: Libdragon 的大部分功能自然适合新平台和渲染后端，尽管我必须更改 high_impact 的一些其他部分以绕过其混合器（Libdragon 有自己的，由 RSP 加速）和图像加载器。

blocks.html_en: Throughout the whole process, I retained the ability to build the game with the SDL2 or Sokol backends. This was great for playtesting game logic and enemy behavior. To make levels, I also implemented a simple hot-reload mechanism triggered whenever a level file changed.

sentences.en: Throughout the whole process, I retained the ability to build the game with the SDL2 or Sokol backends.
sentences.zh: 在整个过程中，我保留了使用 SDL2 或 Sokol 后端构建游戏的能力。

sentences.en: This was great for playtesting game logic and enemy behavior.
sentences.zh: 这对于测试游戏逻辑和敌人行为非常有用。

sentences.en: To make levels, I also implemented a simple hot-reload mechanism triggered whenever a level file changed.
sentences.zh: 为了制作关卡，我还实现了一个简单的热重载机制，每当关卡文件发生更改时就会触发。

I ended up extending it quite a bit to add better support for lightmaps, display actual sprites for entities (instead of just boxes), add descriptions for entity settings and provide other small features. The single source of truth is still the C source code – the level editor reads it and extracts the entity types and supported settings automatically.

sentences.en: The level editor, bundled with high_impact, is a single self-contained HTML file.
sentences.zh: 关卡编辑器与 high_impact 捆绑在一起，是一个独立的 HTML 文件。

sentences.en: I ended up extending it quite a bit to add better support for lightmaps, display actual sprites for entities (instead of just boxes), add descriptions for entity settings and provide other small features.
sentences.zh: 我最终对其进行了相当多的扩展，以添加对光照贴图的更好支持，显示实体的实际精灵（而不仅仅是盒子），添加实体设置的描述并提供其他小功能。

sentences.en: The single source of truth is still the C source code – the level editor reads it and extracts the entity types and supported settings automatically.
sentences.zh: 唯一的事实来源仍然是 C 源代码——关卡编辑器读取它并自动提取实体类型和支持的设置。

sentences.en: The level compiler writes those values in big-endian format for the N64 and little-endian format for x86 (SDL2, Sokol, WASM), so we can easily read everything on all platforms without byte swapping.
sentences.zh: 级别编译器将这些值写入 N64 的大端格式和 x86 的小端格式（SDL2、Sokol、WASM），因此我们可以轻松读取所有平台上的所有内容，而无需进行字节交换。

blocks.html_en: Rendering

sentences.en: Rendering
sentences.zh: 渲染

blocks.html_en: Libdragon itself has a function for drawing triangles: rdpq_triangle() inserts a single triangle draw call into the RDP queue. While this works, what you really want to do is submit your draw calls to the RSP, have some custom microcode to perform transformations, lighting, depth calculations, etc., and then let the RSP instruct the RDP to ultimately draw the triangle.

sentences.en: Libdragon itself has a function for drawing triangles: rdpq_triangle() inserts a single triangle draw call into the RDP queue.
sentences.zh: Libdragon 本身有一个绘制三角形的函数：rdpq_triangle() 将单个三角形绘制调用插入到 RDP 队列中。

sentences.en: While this works, what you really want to do is submit your draw calls to the RSP, have some custom microcode to perform transformations, lighting, depth calculations, etc., and then let the RSP instruct the RDP to ultimately draw the triangle.
sentences.zh: 虽然这可行，但您真正想要做的是将绘制调用提交给 RSP，使用一些自定义微代码来执行转换、照明、深度计算等，然后让 RSP 指示 RDP 最终绘制三角形。

blocks.html_en: The intricacies of the RDP and RSP were still new to me, but luckily another outstanding open-source library, Tiny3D, handles all this and more with a simple-to-use API. Getting something on the screen was the easy part; making it performant was a whole other endeavor.

sentences.en: The intricacies of the RDP and RSP were still new to me, but luckily another outstanding open-source library, Tiny3D, handles all this and more with a simple-to-use API.
sentences.zh: RDP 和 RSP 的复杂性对我来说仍然是新鲜事，但幸运的是，另一个出色的开源库 Tiny3D 通过简单易用的 API 来处理所有这些以及更多内容。

sentences.en: Getting something on the screen was the easy part; making it performant was a whole other endeavor.
sentences.zh: 在屏幕上显示一些内容是比较容易的部分；使其表现出色是另一项完全不同的努力。

blocks.html_en: The N64 infamously only has 4 KB of texture memory. The largest textures you can upload are just a meager 64×64 pixels. Even worse, the memory latency for a texture upload is atrocious. One solution, used by Mario 64 and many other titles, is to render untextured polygons whenever you can.

sentences.en: The N64 infamously only has 4 KB of texture memory.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，N64 的纹理内存只有 4 KB。

sentences.en: The largest textures you can upload are just a meager 64×64 pixels.
sentences.zh: 您可以上传的最大纹理只有区区 64×64 像素。

sentences.en: Even worse, the memory latency for a texture upload is atrocious.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，纹理上传的内存延迟非常严重。

sentences.en: One solution, used by Mario 64 and many other titles, is to render untextured polygons whenever you can.
sentences.zh: Mario 64 和许多其他游戏使用的一种解决方案是尽可能渲染无纹理的多边形。

blocks.html_en: This wouldn't really fly with the style of my game, so instead I had to be really careful with the draw order of level tiles to minimize texture uploads. On top of that, Tiny3D can load and submit up to 17 quads at once, and it would be wasteful not to use that. So I ended up collecting batches of triangles with the same texture in 64-bit draw calls:

sentences.en: This wouldn't really fly with the style of my game, so instead I had to be really careful with the draw order of level tiles to minimize texture uploads.
sentences.zh: 这不太符合我的游戏风格，因此我必须非常小心关卡图块的绘制顺序，以最大程度地减少纹理上传。

sentences.en: On top of that, Tiny3D can load and submit up to 17 quads at once, and it would be wasteful not to use that.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，Tiny3D 可以一次加载和提交最多 17 个四边形，不使用它会很浪费。

sentences.en: So I ended up collecting batches of triangles with the same texture in 64-bit draw calls:
sentences.zh: 因此，我最终在 64 位绘制调用中收集了一批具有相同纹理的三角形：

blocks.html_en: Here vbi is the accompanying vertex buffer index, and len is the number of quads in this call. Since every call is just 64 bits wide, we can efficiently sort them at the end of the frame and issue them to Tiny3D.

sentences.en: Here vbi is the accompanying vertex buffer index, and len is the number of quads in this call.
sentences.zh: 这里 vbi 是伴随的顶点缓冲区索引，len 是本次调用中的四边形数量。

sentences.en: Since every call is just 64 bits wide, we can efficiently sort them at the end of the frame and issue them to Tiny3D.
sentences.zh: 由于每个调用只有 64 位宽，因此我们可以在帧末尾有效地对它们进行排序并将它们发送给 Tiny3D。

blocks.html_en: But before I could do all this, I had to first figure out which parts of a level are actually visible. The original JavaScript Xibalba used a portal system, dividing each level into sectors and precomputing which sectors were visible from the current one. This worked fine, but produced a bit more overdraw than I would have liked.

sentences.en: But before I could do all this, I had to first figure out which parts of a level are actually visible.
sentences.zh: 但在我完成这一切之前，我必须首先弄清楚关卡的哪些部分实际上是可见的。

sentences.en: The original JavaScript Xibalba used a portal system, dividing each level into sectors and precomputing which sectors were visible from the current one.
sentences.zh: 最初的 JavaScript Xibalba 使用门户系统，将每个级别划分为多个扇区，并预先计算哪些扇区对当前扇区可见。

sentences.en: This worked fine, but produced a bit more overdraw than I would have liked.
sentences.zh: 这工作得很好，但产生的透支比我想要的要多一些。

blocks.html_en: So I opted for another approach: raycasting. Yes, the game is just casting 320 rays into the scene, covering the whole field of view. Each ray marks traversed tiles in a bitmap for submission to the renderer.

sentences.en: So I opted for another approach: raycasting.
sentences.zh: 所以我选择了另一种方法：光线投射。

sentences.en: Yes, the game is just casting 320 rays into the scene, covering the whole field of view.
sentences.zh: 是的，游戏只是将 320 条光线投射到场景中，覆盖整个视野。

sentences.en: Each ray marks traversed tiles in a bitmap for submission to the renderer.
sentences.zh: 每条光线都会在位图中标记经过的图块，以便提交给渲染器。

blocks.html_en: Later, I optimized the raycasting a bit more by recursively dividing the 320-pixel field of view until two rays hit the same tile. In this process, I also check whether any of the traversed tiles are missing a ceiling – if so, we have to draw a skybox.

sentences.en: Later, I optimized the raycasting a bit more by recursively dividing the 320-pixel field of view until two rays hit the same tile.
sentences.zh: 后来，我通过递归划分 320 像素视野，直到两条光线击中同一个图块，进一步优化了光线投射。

sentences.en: In this process, I also check whether any of the traversed tiles are missing a ceiling – if so, we have to draw a skybox.
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，我还检查是否有任何遍历的图块缺少天花板 - 如果是这样，我们必须绘制一个天空盒。

blocks.html_en: Fun fact: the skybox in Xibalba 64 is just a single 32×32-pixel texture that is beautifully smeared across the horizon.

sentences.en: Fun fact: the skybox in Xibalba 64 is just a single 32×32-pixel texture that is beautifully smeared across the horizon.
sentences.zh: 有趣的事实：Xibalba 64 中的天空盒只是一个 32×32 像素的纹理，美丽地涂抹在地平线上。

blocks.html_en: As another optimization, I arranged each tile sheet that wouldn't fit in a single upload into a single column and tried to use just 4-bit indexed colors wherever possible. Using fewer colors allowed more pixels to fit into texture memory, and the column layout ensured that each tile could be uploaded as a single, continuous chunk of memory.

sentences.en: As another optimization, I arranged each tile sheet that wouldn't fit in a single upload into a single column and tried to use just 4-bit indexed colors wherever possible.
sentences.zh: 作为另一项优化，我将不适合单次上传的每个图块表安排到单个列中，并尝试尽可能仅使用 4 位索引颜色。

sentences.en: Using fewer colors allowed more pixels to fit into texture memory, and the column layout ensured that each tile could be uploaded as a single, continuous chunk of memory.
sentences.zh: 使用更少的颜色可以让更多的像素适合纹理内存，并且列布局确保每个图块可以作为单个连续的内存块上传。

blocks.html_en: With all of this, the game runs at a stable 60 FPS. Something not many other N64 games can claim!

sentences.en: With all of this, the game runs at a stable 60 FPS.
sentences.zh: 有了这一切，游戏就能以稳定的 60 FPS 运行。

sentences.en: Something not many other N64 games can claim!
sentences.zh: 这是许多其他 N64 游戏所无法比拟的！

blocks.html_en: The four-player split-screen mode doesn't quite hit the 60 FPS mark at all times, but still remains fluid. In contrast, GoldenEye 007 infamously often dropped into single-digit frame rates here.

sentences.en: The four-player split-screen mode doesn't quite hit the 60 FPS mark at all times, but still remains fluid.
sentences.zh: 四人分屏模式并未始终达到 60 FPS 标记，但仍然保持流畅。

sentences.en: In contrast, GoldenEye 007 infamously often dropped into single-digit frame rates here.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，《黄金眼 007》的帧速率经常下降到个位数，这是臭名昭著的。

blocks.html_en: Sound & Music

sentences.en: Sound & Music
sentences.zh: 声音与音乐

blocks.html_en: As with all my other games, my good friend Andreas Lösch produced some outstanding music. You can listen to the whole Xibalba 64 Soundtrack on Bandcamp.

sentences.en: As with all my other games, my good friend Andreas Lösch produced some outstanding music.
sentences.zh: 与我的所有其他游戏一样，我的好朋友 Andreas Lösch 制作了一些出色的音乐。

sentences.en: You can listen to the whole Xibalba 64 Soundtrack on Bandcamp.
sentences.zh: 您可以在 Bandcamp 上收听整个 Xibalba 64 原声带。

blocks.html_en: The game itself also has a built-in music player that you can unlock in the single-player campaign.

sentences.en: The game itself also has a built-in music player that you can unlock in the single-player campaign.
sentences.zh: 游戏本身还具有内置音乐播放器，您可以在单人战役中解锁。

blocks.html_en: Cartridge space is tight, and even compressed audio is typically either quite large or too expensive to decode.

sentences.en: Cartridge space is tight, and even compressed audio is typically either quite large or too expensive to decode.
sentences.zh: 盒带空间很紧张，甚至压缩的音频通常要么很大，要么解码成本太高。

blocks.html_en: In a heroic effort, Giovanni Bajo – one of the maintainers of Libdragon and an absolute wizard when it comes to anything N64 – implemented an RSP-accelerated Opus decoder. For context: Opus is an audio codec first published in 2012. That's 16 years(!) after the N64. It's a marvel that it works at all, but sadly it's still a bit too computationally expensive to be used during gameplay.

sentences.en: In a heroic effort, Giovanni Bajo – one of the maintainers of Libdragon and an absolute wizard when it comes to anything N64 – implemented an RSP-accelerated Opus decoder.
sentences.zh: Giovanni Bajo（Libdragon 的维护者之一，在涉及 N64 方面绝对是奇才）做出了英勇的努力，实现了 RSP 加速的 Opus 解码器。

sentences.en: For context: Opus is an audio codec first published in 2012.
sentences.zh: 背景信息：Opus 是一种音频编解码器，于 2012 年首次发布。

sentences.en: That's 16 years(!)
after the N64.
sentences.zh: N64之后。

sentences.en: It's a marvel that it works at all, but sadly it's still a bit too computationally expensive to be used during gameplay.
sentences.zh: 它能起作用真是一个奇迹，但遗憾的是，在游戏过程中使用它的计算成本仍然有点太高了。

blocks.html_en: (Aside: Giovanni Bajo went on to implement a real-time H.264 decoder for the N64, too.)

sentences.en: (Aside: Giovanni Bajo went on to implement a real-time H.264 decoder for the N64, too.)
sentences.zh: （旁白：Giovanni Bajo 还继续为 N64 实现了实时 H.264 解码器。）

blocks.html_en: The better option for now is a simple 4-bit VADPCM format that Libdragon transparently decodes on the RSP during playback. The compression ratio, of course, isn't great, but it's way better than uncompressed WAV. About 31 MB of the 32 MB ROM is used by sound and music.

sentences.en: The better option for now is a simple 4-bit VADPCM format that Libdragon transparently decodes on the RSP during playback.
sentences.zh: 目前更好的选择是简单的 4 位 VADPCM 格式，Libdragon 在播放期间在 RSP 上透明解码。

sentences.en: The compression ratio, of course, isn't great, but it's way better than uncompressed WAV.
sentences.zh: 当然，压缩率不是很高，但比未压缩的 WAV 好得多。

sentences.en: About 31 MB of the 32 MB ROM is used by sound and music.
sentences.zh: 32 MB ROM 中大约有 31 MB 用于声音和音乐。

blocks.html_en: After the release of Xibalba 64, I started to implement another audio compression format that would better address the space/quality/complexity trade-off. More on that in the next blog post!

sentences.en: After the release of Xibalba 64, I started to implement another audio compression format that would better address the space/quality/complexity trade-off.
sentences.zh: Xibalba 64 发布后，我开始实现另一种音频压缩格式，可以更好地解决空间/质量/复杂性的权衡。

sentences.en: More on that in the next blog post!
sentences.zh: 下一篇博客文章将详细介绍这一点！

sentences.en: Publishing & Sales
sentences.zh: 出版及销售

blocks.html_en: Modretro previously made a Game Boy Color clone – the Chromatic – compatible with all existing Game Boy and Game Boy Color games, and they were quite eager to publish many new games by hobbyist developers, too.

sentences.en: Modretro previously made a Game Boy Color clone – the Chromatic – compatible with all existing Game Boy and Game Boy Color games, and they were quite eager to publish many new games by hobbyist developers, too.
sentences.zh: Modretro 之前制作了 Game Boy Color 克隆版——Chromatic——与所有现有的 Game Boy 和 Game Boy Color 游戏兼容，并且他们也非常渴望发布由业余开发者开发的许多新游戏。

blocks.html_en: When they announced the M64, I thought this would be a great chance to get on board. As soon as I had a working prototype ready and was confident that I would be able to build the whole game (and make it good), I wrote an email to the generic Modretro customer service address and, to my surprise, heard back from the head of publishing within a day.

sentences.en: When they announced the M64, I thought this would be a great chance to get on board.
sentences.zh: 当他们宣布推出 M64 时，我认为这将是一个加入的绝佳机会。

sentences.en: As soon as I had a working prototype ready and was confident that I would be able to build the whole game (and make it good), I wrote an email to the generic Modretro customer service address and, to my surprise, heard back from the head of publishing within a day.
sentences.zh: 当我准备好工作原型并确信自己能够构建整个游戏（并使其变得优秀）时，我给通用的 Modretro 客户服务地址写了一封电子邮件，令我惊讶的是，一天之内就收到了发行负责人的回复。

blocks.html_en: Bureaucracy was minimal and the contract was straightforward. I requested some changes that would allow me to release the game engine as open source later on, which Modretro was happy to accommodate.

sentences.en: Bureaucracy was minimal and the contract was straightforward.
sentences.zh: 官僚主义极少，合同也很简单。

sentences.en: I requested some changes that would allow me to release the game engine as open source later on, which Modretro was happy to accommodate.
sentences.zh: 我请求进行一些更改，以便我稍后能够将游戏引擎作为开源发布，Modretro 很乐意满足。

blocks.html_en: Of course, as it goes with these projects, there were some delays and I only received a pre-production M64 late in the development process. But it didn't matter – the M64 worked as advertised; no changes to the game for the M64 were necessary.

sentences.en: Of course, as it goes with these projects, there were some delays and I only received a pre-production M64 late in the development process.
sentences.zh: 当然，随着这些项目的进行，出现了一些延迟，我在开发过程的后期才收到了预生产的 M64。

sentences.en: But it didn't matter – the M64 worked as advertised; no changes to the game for the M64 were necessary.
sentences.zh: 但这并不重要——M64 的工作原理正如广告中所宣传的那样；无需对 M64 的游戏进行任何更改。

blocks.html_en: Modretro also offered help with the box art, but another friend of mine was eager to do this instead. sentences.en: Modretro also offered help with the box art, but another friend of mine was eager to do this instead.

sentences.en: He later told me that, back in the '90s, he was responsible for the packaging of many titles published by Sierra in Germany, including Half-Life.

sentences.en: So it's no surprise that the Xibalba 64 box art turned out great!
sentences.zh: 因此，Xibalba 64 包装盒艺术效果出色也就不足为奇了！

blocks.html_en: For the manual, I supplied text and illustrations to Modretro, and they laid it out for print. Smooth sailing. You can have a look at the PDF manual on the Xibalba 64 store page.

sentences.zh: 对于手册，我向 Modretro 提供了文本和插图，然后他们将其进行打印。

sentences.en: Smooth sailing.
sentences.zh: 一帆风顺。

sentences.en: You can have a look at the PDF manual on the Xibalba 64 store page.
sentences.zh: 您可以在 Xibalba 64 商店页面查看 PDF 手册。

blocks.html_en: I'm not able to talk about sales numbers or my contract with Modretro in detail, and the game was released only a few days ago, but so far it's looking quite good. sentences.en: I'm not able to talk about sales numbers or my contract with Modretro in detail, and the game was released only a few days ago, but so far it's looking quite good.
sentences.zh: 我无法详细谈论销售数字或我与 Modretro 的合同，而且游戏几天前才发布，但到目前为止看起来相当不错。

sentences.en: Of course, making N64 games will probably not let you quit your job, but it looks like it will pay for a few nice holidays.
sentences.zh: 当然，制作 N64 游戏可能不会让你辞去工作，但看起来它可以支付几个美好的假期。

blocks.html_en: Huge thanks to Giovanni Bajo of Libdragon, Max Bebök of Tiny3D, the entire N64brew Discord community and, of course, the Modretro team for pulling this off!

sentences.en: Huge thanks to Giovanni Bajo of Libdragon, Max Bebök of Tiny3D, the entire N64brew Discord community and, of course, the Modretro team for pulling this off!
sentences.zh: 非常感谢 Libdragon 的 Giovanni Bajo、Tiny3D 的 Max Bebök、整个 N64brew Discord 社区，当然还有 Modretro 团队，感谢他们的帮助！

content_html_zh:
— 2026 年 8 月 4 日星期二

两年前，我无缘无故地将我的 JavaScript 游戏引擎移植到 C。 我从此找到了一个理由：制作一款新的N64游戏！

结果就是 Xibalba 64——一款类似德军总部 3D 的 FPS。 Modretro 同意将该游戏作为他们的 M64（现代 N64 克隆）的实体发行游戏发布，并配有卡带、包装和手册！

Modretro.com 上的 Xibalba 64

据我所知，这只是自 N64 游戏机最初商业生命结束以来第二次实体发布新游戏。 Bitmap Bureau 出品的臭名昭著的《Xeno Crisis》最初是一款针对 Sega Mega Drive 的新游戏，随后在更多的游戏机上发布，并于 2023 年登陆 N64。 自 2002 年《Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3》以来，N64 上还没有发布过其他新游戏。

发动机

Impact 是我在 2010 年开发的 JavaScript 游戏引擎。 它专为 2D 动作游戏量身定制，可处理图块表、背景地图、精灵和碰撞检测。 它非常简单，但仍然是您想要的任何内容的坚实基础。

两年前我用 C 重写了 Impact。 为什么？ 我不知道。 很有趣。

这个 C 端口 high_impact 有一个“平台后端”的概念。 该平台处理低级管道 - 打开窗口、创建绘图表面、读取输入等。 high_impact 开箱即用，附带两个平台后端（SDL2 和 Sokol），您可以为其中任一平台编译游戏。 这已经使 high_impact 游戏能够在许多不同的设备上运行。

high_impact 中的渲染后端也是模块化的。 您可以使用软件渲染器、OpenGL 或 Metal（适用于 iOS/macOS）来编译游戏。 可以添加对新平台后端或渲染后端的支持，而无需修改引擎的任何其他部分。

N64 游戏的完美起点。

N64 硬件和平台库

N64 是一只古怪的野兽。 除了 93 MHz MIPS CPU（大端！）之外，它还有两个协处理器用于处理图形、声音等：

  • “现实显示处理器”（RDP）——固定功能图形处理器
  • “现实信号处理器”（RSP）——可编程矢量处理器

这两者都位于同一个物理包中，通常称为“现实协处理器”(RCP)。

图片来自 N64Brew Wiki

在 N64 诞生的最初几年，任天堂严密保护 RSP 的使用权。 它由任天堂官方认可的平台库“libultra”独家使用。 直到后来，任天堂才允许游戏工作室为 RSP 编写自定义“微代码”（实际上只是 MIPS 汇编）。

保持硬件正常运行并不是一件简单的事，而且 RDP 的指令也很古怪和复杂。 在裸机上编程你的游戏几乎是不可能的。 近年来，任天堂的官方“libultra”已经进入互联网，但使用它可能会面临版权诉讼的风险。

幸运的是，N64 自制程序场景在过去几年中获得了很大的发展，我们现在有一个非常强大的替代方案：Libdragon。

Libdragon 基本上是 N64 的 SDL。 它提供了绘制精灵和三角形、声音输出、控制器输入等功能。

我只花了几个晚上就在 libdragon 之上为 high_impact 构建了一个新的平台后端。 我用 Biolab Disaster 对此进行了测试。 游戏代码保持不变；性能很一般，但我以最简单的方式使用 N64 硬件。

开发环境

Libdragon 提供编译器以及为 N64 构建 ROM 文件所需的所有其他内容。 安装说明和所有其他文档都很全面且写得很好。 该库附带了许多示例来帮助您入门。

总的来说，与 Libdragon 合作很愉快。 请注意：您可能想要使用预览分支，因为“稳定”主干分支已经无可救药地落后了。

对于测试来说，一个好的模拟器是无价的。 在很长一段时间里，N64 仿真极其不准确。 尤其是 RSP 和 RDP 协处理器的仿真不佳是大多数问题的根源。

大多数模拟器只是模拟任天堂的平台库 libultra。 他们模拟了绘制三角形的意图，而不是硬件实际执行的操作。 虽然不准确，但这使得早期的模拟成​​为可能。 众所周知，UltraHLE（“超高水平仿真器”）是在 N64 的生命周期内发布的，并引起了很多麻烦和随后的诉讼。

如今，Ares 中的 N64 内核更加接近实际硬件 - RDP 和 RSP 已完全仿真，包括 RSP 的精确计时。 然而，N64 臭名昭著的慢内存带宽仍然只能在真实硬件上进行测试（这最近让我有些失望）。

因此，您需要一个真正的 N64 和一个可以播放任意 .z64 ROM 文件的卡带。 开源的 SummerCart64 非常出色，并且可以从许多不同的制造商处获得。 请注意：一些制造商（尤其是 AliExpress 上的制造商）会以低价出售主板的组件。

SummerCart64 具有常用的 SD 卡插槽来存储 ROM，但它非常适合开发的是其 USB-C 端口：您可以将其直接连接到 PC 并使用 sc64deployer 在构建过程中上传 ROM。

我最终将 N64 放在我的 PC 旁边，通过 USB 连接，并使用便宜的 10 美元 USB 模拟采集卡在桌面上的窗口中显示其视频输出。 在 Linux 上，需要对 mpv 进行一些修改才能获得低延迟输出；这是我使用的脚本。

通过这种设置，在真实硬件上进行迭代只需编译并按下 N64 重置按钮即可。

游戏

我最初在 2014 年制作了 Xibalba 作为我的 JavaScript 游戏引擎的演示。 当时 WebGL 仍然是热门的新事物；浏览器中的 3D 游戏相当新颖。 游戏非常短，只有少数关卡、武器和敌人类型。

相比之下，我希望 Xibalba 64 成为一款真正的游戏，而不仅仅是一个演示版。 因此，我不仅需要将游戏移植到 C 和 high_impact，还需要对其进行扩展，添加更多关卡、更多敌人类型和更多武器。

high_impact 是 2D 游戏引擎，但 Xibalba 64 显然是 3D 游戏引擎。 嗯，不完全是。 由于游戏没有高度，因此可以大部分视为 2D。 从概念上讲，您可以从 2D 自上而下的角度来玩 Xibalba 64。 当然，这不会那么令人兴奋，但所有的物理、运动和射击都会以同样的方式工作。 在这方面，该游戏与德军总部 3D 非常相似。

high_impact 的许多物理函数都需要带有 .x 和 .y 分量的 vec2_t 参数。 但对于绘图，我绝对需要 3D 位置，因此我提出了 vec3_t 类型的定义并更改了entity_t 类型：

typedef struct {
    float x, y;
} vec2_t;

typedef union {
    vec2_t xy;
    struct {
        float x, y, z;
    };
} vec3_t;

typedef struct {
    // ...
    vec3_t pos;
    vec3_t vel;
    // ...
} entity_t;

现在，每当我需要调用接受 vec2_t 的函数时，我都可以免费从 vec3_t “转换”：

trace_t res = trace(collision_map, entity->pos.xy, entity->vel.xy);

由于内部 vec3_t 结构是“匿名的”，我仍然可以直接访问所有值；即，entity->pos.z 工作得很好。

现有关卡和敌人类型的初始移植进展相当顺利，大约两周内就完成了。 然后我又花了几个月的时间来扩展游戏并优化渲染器。

Libdragon 的大部分功能自然适合新平台和渲染后端，尽管我必须更改 high_impact 的一些其他部分以绕过其混合器（Libdragon 有自己的，由 RSP 加速）和图像加载器。

在整个过程中，我保留了使用 SDL2 或 Sokol 后端构建游戏的能力。 这对于测试游戏逻辑和敌人行为非常有用。 为了制作关卡，我还实现了一个简单的热重载机制，每当关卡文件发生更改时就会触发。

关卡编辑器与 high_impact 捆绑在一起，是一个独立的 HTML 文件。 我最终对其进行了相当多的扩展，以添加对光照贴图的更好支持，显示实体的实际精灵（而不仅仅是盒子），添加实体设置的描述并提供其他小功能。 唯一的事实来源仍然是 C 源代码——关卡编辑器读取它并自动提取实体类型和支持的设置。

由于关卡编辑器仍然可以使用 JSON 文件，因此我构建了一个小型地图编译器来读取 JSON 并发出二进制数据。 虽然在 N64 上加载 JSON 当然是可能的，但它增加了一些不必要的约 100 毫秒的加载时间。 因此，在构建过程中，每个 JSON 级别文件都会转换为一个结构，其本质上如下所示：

typedef struct {
    uint16_t magic;
    uint16_t entities_len;
    uint16_t map_width;
    uint16_t map_height;

    struct {
        uint16_t type_id;
        uint16_t x;
        uint16_t y;
        uint16_t settings_len;
        struct {
            uint16_t setting_type; // such as "name", "target", "size", ...
            union {
                float16_t float_value;
                int16_t int_value;
                struct {
                    int16_t string_len;
                    char string_value;
                };
            } value;
        } settings[settings_len];
    } entities[entities_len];

    uint16_t collision_map[map_width * map_height];
    uint16_t floor_map[map_width * map_height];
    uint16_t wall_map[map_width * map_height];
    uint16_t ceiling_map[map_width * map_height];
    uint16_t light_map[map_width * map_height];
} level_t;

级别编译器将这些值写入 N64 的大端格式和 x86 的小端格式（SDL2、Sokol、WASM），因此我们可以轻松读取所有平台上的所有内容，而无需进行字节交换。

渲染

Libdragon 本身有一个绘制三角形的函数：rdpq_triangle() 将单个三角形绘制调用插入到 RDP 队列中。 虽然这可行，但您真正想要做的是将绘制调用提交给 RSP，使用一些自定义微代码来执行转换、照明、深度计算等，然后让 RSP 指示 RDP 最终绘制三角形。

RDP 和 RSP 的复杂性对我来说仍然是新鲜事，但幸运的是，另一个出色的开源库 Tiny3D 通过简单易用的 API 来处理所有这些以及更多内容。 在屏幕上显示一些内容是比较容易的部分；使其表现出色是另一项完全不同的努力。

众所周知，N64 的纹理内存只有 4 KB。 您可以上传的最大纹理只有区区 64×64 像素。 更糟糕的是，纹理上传的内存延迟非常严重。 Mario 64 和许多其他游戏使用的一种解决方案是尽可能渲染无纹理的多边形。

这不太符合我的游戏风格，因此我必须非常小心关卡图块的绘制顺序，以最大程度地减少纹理上传。 最重要的是，Tiny3D 可以一次加载和提交最多 17 个四边形，不使用它会很浪费。 因此，我最终在 64 位绘制调用中收集了一批具有相同纹理的三角形：

typedef union render_call {
    uint64_t packed;
    uint32_t hashable;
    uint64_t ident : 46;
    struct {
        uint64_t translucent : 1;
        uint64_t texture_index : 9;
        uint64_t x : 10;
        uint64_t y : 10;
        uint64_t w : 8;
        uint64_t h : 8;
        uint64_t vbi : 14;
        uint64_t len : 4;
    };
} render_call_t;

这里 vbi 是伴随的顶点缓冲区索引，len 是本次调用中的四边形数量。 由于每个调用只有 64 位宽，因此我们可以在帧末尾有效地对它们进行排序并将它们发送给 Tiny3D。

但在我完成这一切之前，我必须首先弄清楚关卡的哪些部分实际上是可见的。 最初的 JavaScript Xibalba 使用门户系统，将每个级别划分为多个扇区，并预先计算哪些扇区对当前扇区可见。 这工作得很好，但产生的透支比我想要的要多一些。

所以我选择了另一种方法：光线投射。 是的，游戏只是将 320 条光线投射到场景中，覆盖整个视野。 每条光线都会在位图中标记经过的图块，以便提交给渲染器。

后来，我通过递归划分 320 像素视野，直到两条光线击中同一个图块，进一步优化了光线投射。 在此过程中，我还检查是否有任何遍历的图块缺少天花板 - 如果是这样，我们必须绘制一个天空盒。

有趣的事实：Xibalba 64 中的天空盒只是一个 32×32 像素的纹理，美丽地涂抹在地平线上。

作为另一项优化，我将不适合单次上传的每个图块表安排到单个列中，并尝试尽可能仅使用 4 位索引颜色。 使用更少的颜色可以让更多的像素适合纹理内存，并且列布局确保每个图块可以作为单个连续的内存块上传。

有了这一切，游戏就能以稳定的 60 FPS 运行。 这是许多其他 N64 游戏所无法比拟的！

四人分屏模式并未始终达到 60 FPS 标记，但仍然保持流畅。 相比之下，《黄金眼 007》的帧速率经常下降到个位数，这是臭名昭著的。

声音与音乐

与我的所有其他游戏一样，我的好朋友 Andreas Lösch 制作了一些出色的音乐。 您可以在 Bandcamp 上收听整个 Xibalba 64 原声带。

游戏本身还具有内置音乐播放器，您可以在单人战役中解锁。

盒带空间很紧张，甚至压缩的音频通常要么很大，要么解码成本太高。

Giovanni Bajo（Libdragon 的维护者之一，在涉及 N64 方面绝对是奇才）做出了英勇的努力，实现了 RSP 加速的 Opus 解码器。 背景信息：Opus 是一种音频编解码器，于 2012 年首次发布。 那是16年（！） N64之后。 它能起作用真是一个奇迹，但遗憾的是，在游戏过程中使用它的计算成本仍然有点太高了。

（旁白：Giovanni Bajo 还继续为 N64 实现了实时 H.264 解码器。）

目前更好的选择是简单的 4 位 VADPCM 格式，Libdragon 在播放期间在 RSP 上透明解码。 当然，压缩率不是很高，但比未压缩的 WAV 好得多。 32 MB ROM 中大约有 31 MB 用于声音和音乐。

Xibalba 64 发布后，我开始实现另一种音频压缩格式，可以更好地解决空间/质量/复杂性的权衡。 下一篇博客文章将详细介绍这一点！

出版及销售

Modretro 之前制作了 Game Boy Color 克隆版——Chromatic——与所有现有的 Game Boy 和 Game Boy Color 游戏兼容，并且他们也非常渴望发布由业余开发者开发的许多新游戏。

当他们宣布推出 M64 时，我认为这将是一个加入的绝佳机会。 当我准备好工作原型并确信自己能够构建整个游戏（并使其变得优秀）时，我给通用的 Modretro 客户服务地址写了一封电子邮件，令我惊讶的是，一天之内就收到了发行负责人的回复。

官僚主义极少，合同也很简单。 我请求进行一些更改，以便我稍后能够将游戏引擎作为开源发布，Modretro 很乐意满足。

当然，随着这些项目的进行，出现了一些延迟，我在开发过程的后期才收到了预生产的 M64。 但这并不重要——M64 的工作原理正如广告中所宣传的那样；无需对 M64 的游戏进行任何更改。

莫德雷特罗还提供了包装盒艺术方面的帮助，但我的另一位朋友却渴望这样做。 他后来告诉我，早在 90 年代，他就负责包装德国 Sierra 出版的许多游戏，包括《半条命》。 因此，Xibalba 64 包装盒艺术效果出色也就不足为奇了！

对于手册，我向 Modretro 提供了文本和插图，然后他们将其进行打印。 一帆风顺。 您可以在 Xibalba 64 商店页面查看 PDF 手册。

我无法详细谈论销售数字或我与 Modretro 的合同，而且游戏几天前才发布，但到目前为止看起来相当不错。 当然，制作 N64 游戏可能不会让你辞去工作，但看起来它可以支付几个美好的假期。

非常感谢 Libdragon 的 Giovanni Bajo、Tiny3D 的 Max Bebök、整个 N64brew Discord 社区，当然还有 Modretro 团队，感谢他们的帮助！

这是游戏的最终预告片。

  • Tiny3D – 一个简单快速的3D图形库
